title: Schizophrenia & Depression: Biological Explanations
welcome_lead: Dopamine and serotonin — the chemistry of two major disorders.
meta_desc: A-Level Psychology schizophrenia dopamine hypothesis depression serotonin biological.
final_note: Same brain, different chemistry, different disorder.

concepts.def: Excess dopamine in subcortical areas — positive symptoms.
Low dopamine in prefrontal cortex — negative symptoms.
Probability one twin has disorder if other does.
Serotonin controls noradrenaline — low serotonin = mood swing.

walkthroughs.body_html: Gottesman (1991) meta-analysed twin studies: schizophrenia concordance is 48% in MZ twins vs 17% in DZ twins, supporting strong genetic component. Ripke et al. (2014): 108 candidate genes — schizophrenia is highly polygenic. Tienari (2004) adopted children of schizophrenic biological mothers were vulnerable but only if raised in dysfunctional families — diathesis-stress.

Amphetamines raise dopamine and induce psychosis; antipsychotics block D2 receptors. Updated hypothesis: hyperdopaminergia in mesolimbic pathway → positive symptoms; hypodopaminergia in mesocortical pathway → negative symptoms. Atypical antipsychotics also target serotonin.

Low serotonin and noradrenaline are linked to depression — SSRIs raise serotonin and reduce symptoms in 60-70% of cases (Kirsch 2008 disputes). HPA axis dysregulation causes high cortisol. Heritability of major depression is around 40% (Sullivan 2000).
